beats.say: In weight-space programming, a frontier model writes a network's weights directly instead of training it. Claude Fable 5.2 had to set all 5,994 weights of an image classifier by hand.
Its first attempt scored about 71 percent accuracy on handwritten digits, beating 500 steps of Adam at 55 percent — though it is not quite a like-for-like comparison.
The lesson is historical: the model reaches for 1990s techniques like hand-drawn templates and stroke detectors.

hook: An AI hand-wrote every weight of a neural network.
